analyst_view.overall: A relegation six-pointer: Coventry are 17th under Frank Lampard, two points above bottom side Palace, who have lost four straight league games and have the worst defence in the division. Palace sacked Pierre Sage during the break and this is Thomas Frank's first match in charge, something the numbers can't see. Mateta is banned (three games, counted) and Strand Larsen (ankle) was back in training on Tuesday and could play, otherwise Palace have no recognised centre-forward; Sarr and Tomiyasu were listed with a 21 November return, so their status is unclear. Coventry are missing Haji Wright (counted). Referee Darren England is slightly above average for cards (counted). I lean a little lower on goals for a new manager's first game and a little higher on cards for the stakes.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, already counting Mateta's ban and Palace's leaky recent defence. A new manager's first game usually starts with a tighter defensive shape, and Palace may be without any fit striker if Strand Larsen isn't ready; Coventry also lack Haji Wright. So a mild trim to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Frank's sides lean on set pieces and direct play, but one week of training won't change Palace's game much, and Coventry's style at home is already in their figures; so I stay at about 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, low for a game between 17th and 20th, already counting referee Darren England (4.2 a game). A nervous six-pointer with Palace players trying to impress a new manager usually brings a few more fouls, so a mild lean up to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, pushed up by how many shots Palace have been conceding lately. A new manager will first try to stop that, and Palace's own volume suffers if Strand Larsen is missing alongside Mateta; so about 26.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Without a recognised striker Palace's shots tend to come from distance, and a more cautious first game under Frank trims it a little, to about 7.8.
